before.title: Smooth composition, difference, coefficient product and commutator estimates on bounded H^s data
before.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$, $k:=s-1\ge4$, let
$O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be open, let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval, let
$F:I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times O\to\mathbb R^{m'}$ and
$A:I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times O\to M_{m'}(\mathbb R)$ be smooth, let
$K\subseteq O$ be compact and let $R\ge0$. Then there is
$C=C(F,A,s,m,m',K,R)$ such that for every $u:I\to H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$
with $u(t)(x)\in K$ and $\|u(t)\|_{H^s}\le R$ for all $t$, the following hold,
where compositions use the continuous representatives of
[[lem-gr-periodic-sobolev-embedding]]:

**(a)** for every integer $0\le r\le s$, $\|F(t,\cdot,u(t))\|_{H^r}\le C\,(1+\|u(t)\|_{H^s})$;

**(b)** if $C_1\subseteq O$ is compact and convex, $u,v$ take values in $C_1$
and $\|v(t)\|_{H^s}\le R$, then
$$\|F(t,\cdot,u(t))-F(t,\cdot,v(t))\|_{H^k}\le C\,\|u(t)-v(t)\|_{H^k};$$

**(c)** for every $1\le|\alpha|\le k$ and every $w\in H^{|\alpha|-1}$,
$$\bigl\|D^\alpha\bigl(A(t,\cdot,u(t))\,w\bigr)-A(t,\cdot,u(t))\,D^\alpha w\bigr\|_2\le C\,\bigl(1+\|w\|_{H^{|\alpha|-1}}\bigr);$$

**(d)** for every $0\le j\le k$ and every $w\in H^j$, $\|A(t,\cdot,u(t))\,w\|_{H^j}\le C\,\|w\|_{H^j}$.

references.title: H. Friedrich and A. D. Rendall, The Cauchy Problem for the Einstein Equations, Living Reviews in Relativity 3 (2000), article 1 (arXiv:gr-qc/0002074), Section 3.1 (Symmetric Hyperbolic Systems): the definition of a quasilinear symmetric hyperbolic system, the finite-dimensional mollifier approximation (3.1) solved by ODE theory, the energy and Moser product/composition estimates, the higher-order energy inequality, uniqueness, the Rellich/Ascoli compactness step and the passage to a classical solution, with Remarks 1-6 on smooth persistence, the continuation criterion, Cauchy stability and the non-identity time matrix

J. K. Hunter, Notes on Partial Differential Equations (UC Davis lecture notes), Chapter 3 (Sobolev Spaces), Sections 3.1 (weak derivatives), 3.4 (properties of weak derivatives), 3.5 (Sobolev spaces), 3.7-3.8 (Sobolev embedding) and 3.10 (compactness results)

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$, let $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be open, let $I$ be an open time interval, let $I_0\subseteq I$ be a compact interval, and let $F:I\times\mathbb T^3\times O\to\mathbb R^{m'}$ and $A:I\times\mathbb T^3\times O\to M_{m'}(\mathbb R)$ be smooth. Fix compact $K\subseteq O$ and $R\ge0$. Constants below depend on these data and are uniform in $t\in I_0$. For $u,v\in H^s$ with values in $K$ and norms at most $R$:

**(a)** $\|F(t,\cdot,u)\|_{H^j}\le C(1+\|u\|_{H^s})$ for $0\le j\le s$.

**(b)** $\|F(t,\cdot,u)-F(t,\cdot,v)\|_{H^{s-1}}\le C\|u-v\|_{H^{s-1}}$. The same bound holds at order zero.

**(c)** For $1\le j=|\alpha|\le s-1$, $\|[D^\alpha,A(t,\cdot,u)]w\|_2\le C\|w\|_{H^{j-1}}$. For $|\alpha|=s$, $\|[D^\alpha,A(t,\cdot,u)]w\|_2\le C\|w\|_{H^{s-1}}$. Commutators are interpreted distributionally by their Leibniz expansion, even if the two individual order-$j$ terms are not separately in $L^2$.

**(d)** For $0\le j\le s-1$, $\|A(t,\cdot,u)w\|_{H^j}\le C\|w\|_{H^j}$.

**(e)** Let $n\ge6$, $\rho\ge0$ and $z\in H^n$ with values in $K$ and $\|z\|_{H^{n-1}}\le\rho$. Then $\|F(t,\cdot,z)\|_{H^n}\le C_\rho(1+\|z\|_{H^n})$. Moreover for $w\in H^{n-1}$ and $|\alpha|\le n$,
$$\|[D^\alpha,A(t,\cdot,z)]w\|_2\le C_\rho\bigl(\|w\|_{H^{n-1}}+(1+\|z\|_{H^n})\|w\|_{H^{n-2}}\bigr).$$
The same estimates apply to any smooth coefficient obtained from $F,A$ by differentiation or by a smooth matrix inverse where that inverse exists on a neighborhood of $I_0\times\mathbb T^3\times K$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let integers $s\ge m\ge0$ satisfy $s-m>3/2$, and
let $u\in H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ with the objects and notation of
[[def-gr-periodic-torus-and-sobolev-spaces]]. Then:

**(a)** There is a unique representative $u^*\in C^m(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$
of the class $u$, and for every $|\alpha|\le m$ the series
$\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^3}(ik)^\alpha\widehat u(k)\chi_k$ converges absolutely and
uniformly on $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ to $D^\alpha u^*$; moreover there is
$C=C(s,m,N)$ with
$$\|u^*\|_{C^m}\le C\,\|u\|_{H^s}.$$

**(b)** Writing $d(x,y):=\min\{\,|x-y+2\pi l|:l\in\mathbb Z^3\,\}$ for the
induced metric on $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ and fixing
$0<\theta\le\min\{1,s-m-\tfrac32\}$, there is $C'=C'(s,m,N,\theta)$ with
$$\bigl|D^\alpha u^*(x)-D^\alpha u^*(y)\bigr|\le C'\,\|u\|_{H^s}\,d(x,y)^\theta\qquad(x,y\in\mathbb T^3_{2\pi},\ |\alpha|\le m).$$

**(c)** The assignment $u\mapsto u^*$ is linear; and if $(u_j)$ is a sequence in
$H^s$ with $u_j\to u$ in $H^s$, then $u_j^*\to u^*$ uniformly together with all
derivatives of order at most $m$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]) for the quotient, product-measure and integration
clauses below, as in [[def-the-one-dimensional-torus-and-normalized-haar-integral]].

**(a) The 2 pi-periodic torus.** Let $\mathbb T_{2\pi}:=\mathbb R/2\pi\mathbb Z$
carry the quotient topology, and let
$$\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}:=\mathbb T_{2\pi}\times\mathbb T_{2\pi}\times\mathbb T_{2\pi}$$
with the product topology; write $q:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ for the
quotient map and $[x]:=(x^1+2\pi\mathbb Z,x^2+2\pi\mathbb Z,x^3+2\pi\mathbb Z)$.
The map $[0,2\pi)^3\to\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$, $x\mapsto[x]$, is a bijection. The
normalized product measure $\mu$ is $\mu_{\mathbb T}\otimes\mu_{\mathbb T}\otimes\mu_{\mathbb T}$,
where $\mu_{\mathbb T}$ is the normalized measure of
[[def-the-one-dimensional-torus-and-normalized-haar-integral]] transported by
$t\mapsto2\pi t$; it is a probability measure on the Borel sets of
$\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ and $\int f\,d\mu=(2\pi)^{-3}\int_{[0,2\pi)^3}f\circ q\,d\lambda_3$
for bounded measurable $f$ ([[thm-tonelli-theorem-for-sigma-finite-product-spaces]]).

**(b) Test functions and continuous classes.** For $N\ge1$ let
$C^\infty(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ be the set of compositions
$u\circ q$ of smooth maps $u:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^N$ that are $2\pi$-periodic
in each variable; these are the **smooth test functions** (real-valued when
$N=1$). For $m\ge0$ let $C^m(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ be the set of
$u\circ q$ with $u\in C^m(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^N)$ $2\pi$-periodic in each
variable ([[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]), with
$$\|u\|_{C^m}:=\max_{|\alpha|\le m}\ \sup_{x\in\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}}\bigl|(D^\alpha u)(x)\bigr| ,$$
where $D^\alpha$ is the multi-index derivative of
[[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]] applied to any
periodic representative; the displayed expression is independent of the
representative.

**(c) The Hilbert space $L^2$.** For $N\ge1$ let
$L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ be the quotient of the set of measurable
$u$ with $\int|u|^2\,d\mu<\infty$ by the $\mu$-a.e. zero functions
([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]],
[[thm-the-l-p-norm-descends-to-the-quotient-and-makes-l-p-a-normed-space]]),
with inner product $\langle u,v\rangle_2=\int u\cdot v\,d\mu$ and norm
$\|u\|_2=\langle u,u\rangle_2^{1/2}$; it is a real Hilbert space
([[lem-l-two-with-the-integral-pairing-is-a-hilbert-space]]). For
$u\in L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ and $k\in\mathbb Z^3$ the
**$k$-th Fourier coefficient** is the vector
$$\widehat u(k):=\int_{\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}}u(x)\,e^{-ik\cdot x}\,d\mu(x)\in\mathbb C^N ,$$
where $e^{-ik\cdot x}:=\chi_{-k}$ with $\chi_k([x]):=\exp(i\,k\cdot x)$; here
$u$ is read through any representative. Write $\chi_k:\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\to\mathbb C$,
$k\in\mathbb Z^3$, for these **characters**; under the identification
$x=2\pi y$ they are the characters $\exp(2\pi i\,k\cdot y)$ of
[[thm-fourier-basis-and-parseval-on-the-n-torus]], so $(\chi_k)_{k\in\mathbb Z^3}$
is an orthonormal basis of the complex space $L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb C)$.

**(d) Weak derivatives and the periodic Sobolev spaces.** For
$u,v\in L^1(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R)$ and $\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^3$ say that
$v$ is the **weak derivative** $D^\alpha u$ if
$$\int_{\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}}u\,D^\alpha\varphi\,d\mu=(-1)^{|\alpha|}\int_{\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}}v\,\varphi\,d\mu$$
for every $\varphi\in C^\infty(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R)$, where $D^\alpha\varphi$
is the multi-index derivative of the periodic representative
([[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]] records the
Euclidean analogue). For an integer $s\ge0$ let
$$H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N):=\Bigl\{u\in L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N):\ \text{for every }|\alpha|\le s\text{ there is }v_\alpha\in L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)\text{ with }v_\alpha=D^\alpha u\Bigr\},$$
the vector-valued weak derivative being componentwise, and put
$$\|u\|_{H^s}:=\Bigl(\sum_{|\alpha|\le s}\|D^\alpha u\|_2^2\Bigr)^{1/2}.$$
The classes $L^2\subseteq L^1$ on the probability space, so the integrals in the
test identity are finite: $|\int u\,D^\alpha\varphi\,d\mu|\le\|u\|_2\|D^\alpha\varphi\|_2$
by Cauchy--Schwarz. The definition asserts neither that the weak derivative
exists nor that the two norms compared in the next item are equivalent; those
are proved in [[lem-gr-periodic-fourier-differentiation-and-norm-equivalence]].

**(e) Conventions.** $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ open, $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ an
interval and maps $F:I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times O\to\mathbb R^{m'}$ are
called smooth when their representatives $F(t,q(x),u)=G(t,x,u)$ have
$G\in C^\infty$. Throughout this page the torus is always this
$2\pi$-periodic one; a statement "for every $x$" means for every point of
$\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$, and "a.e." means $\mu$-a.e.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $k\ge4$ be an integer and let
$u,v\in H^k(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R)$ with the objects and notation of
[[def-gr-periodic-torus-and-sobolev-spaces]]. Then:

**(a)** For every $|\gamma|\le k-2$ the weak derivative $D^\gamma u$ has a
continuous representative and
$$\sup_{x\in\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}}|D^\gamma u(x)|\le C_k\|u\|_{H^k},$$
with $C_k$ depending only on $k$;

**(b)** the pointwise product $uv$ of the continuous representatives lies in
$H^k$ and
$$\|uv\|_{H^k}\le C_k\,\|u\|_{H^k}\,\|v\|_{H^k};$$

**(c)** if $\varphi\in C^k(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R)$ and
$w\in H^k(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R)$, then $\varphi w\in H^k$ and
$$\|\varphi w\|_{H^k}\le C_k\,\|\varphi\|_{C^k}\,\|w\|_{H^k}.$$

Let $m\ge1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be open, and let $f:U\to\mathbb R$. A **multi-index** is $\alpha=(\alpha_0,\ldots,\alpha_{m-1})\in\mathbb N^m$. Put

$$|\alpha|:=\sum_{i<m}\alpha_i,\qquad \alpha!:=\prod_{i<m}\alpha_i!,\qquad h^\alpha:=\prod_{i<m}h_i^{\alpha_i}\quad(h\in\mathbb R^m).$$

Here $|\alpha|$ and $\alpha!$ use the natural-number sum and product of [[def-nat-finite-sum-and-product]], and $n!$ is the factorial of [[def-factorial-and-falling-factorial]]. By contrast, $h^\alpha$ is the finite product in $\mathbb R$ of [[def-finite-sum]], with the natural exponents interpreted by [[def-integer-power]]. For the zero multi-index $0$, set $D^0f:=f$. For nonzero $\alpha$, write

$$D^\alpha f:=\partial_0^{\alpha_0}\cdots\partial_{m-1}^{\alpha_{m-1}}f$$

for this displayed, canonical order whenever it exists. Coordinate partial derivatives have the meaning fixed in [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]].

For $k\in\mathbb N$, $f$ is of class $C^k$ on $U$ when, for every word $(i_1,\ldots,i_r)$ of coordinate indices with $0\le r\le k$, the iterated derivative $\partial_{i_r}\cdots\partial_{i_1}f$ exists and is continuous on $U$; the word of length $0$ denotes $f$. Thus this definition does **not** presuppose that differently ordered derivatives are equal. Equality of their values is a later theorem under these regularity hypotheses.

([[lem-l-two-with-the-integral-pairing-is-a-hilbert-space]]). For
$u\in L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ and $k\in\mathbb Z^3$ the
**$k$-th Fourier coefficient** is the vector
$$\widehat u(k):=\int_{\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}}u(x)\,e^{-ik\cdot x}\,d\mu(x)\in\mathbb C^N ,$$
where $e^{-ik\cdot x}:=\chi_{-k}$ with $\chi_k([x]):=\exp(i\,k\cdot x)$; here
$u$ is read through any representative. Write $\chi_k:\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\to\mathbb C$,
$k\in\mathbb Z^3$, for these **characters**; under the identification
$x=2\pi y$ they are the characters $\exp(2\pi i\,k\cdot y)$ of
[[thm-fourier-basis-and-parseval-on-the-n-torus]], so $(\chi_k)_{k\in\mathbb Z^3}$
is an orthonormal basis of the complex space $L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb C)$.

**(d) Weak derivatives and the periodic Sobolev spaces.** For
$u,v\in L^1(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R)$ and $\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^3$ say that
$v$ is the **weak derivative** $D^\alpha u$ if
$$\int_{\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}}u\,D^\alpha\varphi\,d\mu=(-1)^{|\alpha|}\int_{\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}}v\,\varphi\,d\mu$$
for every $\varphi\in C^\infty(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R)$, where $D^\alpha\varphi$
is the multi-index derivative of the periodic representative
([[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]] records the
Euclidean analogue). For an integer $s\ge0$ let
$$H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N):=\Bigl\{u\in L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N):\ \text{for every }|\alpha|\le s\text{ there is }v_\alpha\in L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)\text{ with }v_\alpha=D^\alpha u\Bigr\},$$
the vector-valued weak derivative being componentwise, and put
$$\|u\|_{H^s}:=\Bigl(\sum_{|\alpha|\le s}\|D^\alpha u\|_2^2\Bigr)^{1/2}.$$
The classes $L^2\subseteq L^1$ on the probability space, so the integrals in the
test identity are finite: $|\int u\,D^\alpha\varphi\,d\mu|\le\|u\|_2\|D^\alpha\varphi\|_2$
by Cauchy--Schwarz. The definition asserts neither that the weak derivative
exists nor that the two norms compared in the next item are equivalent; those
are proved in [[lem-gr-periodic-fourier-differentiation-and-norm-equivalence]].

**(e) Conventions.** $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ open, $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ an
interval and maps $F:I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times O\to\mathbb R^{m'}$ are
called smooth when their representatives $F(t,q(x),u)=G(t,x,u)$ have
$G\in C^\infty$. Throughout this page the torus is always this
$2\pi$-periodic one; a statement "for every $x$" means for every point of
$\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$, and "a.e." means $\mu$-a.e.

after.quote:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let integers $s\ge m\ge0$ satisfy $s-m>3/2$, and
let $u\in H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$ with the objects and notation of
[[def-gr-periodic-torus-and-sobolev-spaces]]. Then:

**(a)** There is a unique representative $u^*\in C^m(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^N)$
of the class $u$, and for every $|\alpha|\le m$ the series
$\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^3}(ik)^\alpha\widehat u(k)\chi_k$ converges absolutely and
uniformly on $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ to $D^\alpha u^*$; moreover there is
$C=C(s,m,N)$ with
$$\|u^*\|_{C^m}\le C\,\|u\|_{H^s}.$$

**(b)** Writing $d(x,y):=\min\{\,|x-y+2\pi l|:l\in\mathbb Z^3\,\}$ for the
induced metric on $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ and fixing
$0<\theta\le\min\{1,s-m-\tfrac32\}$, there is $C'=C'(s,m,N,\theta)$ with
$$\bigl|D^\alpha u^*(x)-D^\alpha u^*(y)\bigr|\le C'\,\|u\|_{H^s}\,d(x,y)^\theta\qquad(x,y\in\mathbb T^3_{2\pi},\ |\alpha|\le m).$$

**(c)** The assignment $u\mapsto u^*$ is linear; and if $(u_j)$ is a sequence in
$H^s$ with $u_j\to u$ in $H^s$, then $u_j^*\to u^*$ uniformly together with all
derivatives of order at most $m$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $k\ge4$ be an integer and let
$u,v\in H^k(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R)$ with the objects and notation of
[[def-gr-periodic-torus-and-sobolev-spaces]]. Then:

**(a)** For every $|\gamma|\le k-2$ the weak derivative $D^\gamma u$ has a
continuous representative and
$$\sup_{x\in\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}}|D^\gamma u(x)|\le C_k\|u\|_{H^k},$$
with $C_k$ depending only on $k$;

**(b)** the pointwise product $uv$ of the continuous representatives lies in
$H^k$ and
$$\|uv\|_{H^k}\le C_k\,\|u\|_{H^k}\,\|v\|_{H^k};$$

**(c)** if $\varphi\in C^k(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R)$ and
$w\in H^k(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R)$, then $\varphi w\in H^k$ and
$$\|\varphi w\|_{H^k}\le C_k\,\|\varphi\|_{C^k}\,\|w\|_{H^k}.$$

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $m\ge1$, $N\ge0$, and let $P_N$ be the Galerkin
projection and $X_N$ the Galerkin space of [[def-gr-galerkin-fourier-projection]]
on $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$. Then:

**(a)** $P_N$ is linear on $L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$, self-adjoint
($\langle P_Nu,v\rangle_2=\langle u,P_Nv\rangle_2$ for all $u,v\in L^2$) and
idempotent ($P_N^2=P_N$), with range $X_N$ and kernel the classes with vanishing
coefficients on $\Lambda_N$;

**(b)** for every multi-index $\alpha$ with $|\alpha|\le s$ and every
$u\in H^s$, $P_ND^\alpha u=D^\alpha P_Nu$;

**(c)** for every $0\le r\le s$ and every $u\in H^r$,
$\|P_Nu\|_{H^r}\le\|u\|_{H^r}$;

**(d)** for every $0\le r\le s$ and every $u\in H^r$, $P_Nu\to u$ in $H^r$ as
$N\to\infty$;

**(e)** for every $s\ge1$, every $u\in H^s$ and every $N\ge0$,
$$\|u-P_Nu\|_{H^{s-1}}\le C_s\,(1+N^2)^{-1/2}\,\|u\|_{H^s}$$
with $C_s$ depending only on $s$.

Let $m\ge1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be open, and let $f:U\to\mathbb R$. A **multi-index** is $\alpha=(\alpha_0,\ldots,\alpha_{m-1})\in\mathbb N^m$. Put

$$|\alpha|:=\sum_{i<m}\alpha_i,\qquad \alpha!:=\prod_{i<m}\alpha_i!,\qquad h^\alpha:=\prod_{i<m}h_i^{\alpha_i}\quad(h\in\mathbb R^m).$$

Here $|\alpha|$ and $\alpha!$ use the natural-number sum and product of [[def-nat-finite-sum-and-product]], and $n!$ is the factorial of [[def-factorial-and-falling-factorial]]. By contrast, $h^\alpha$ is the finite product in $\mathbb R$ of [[def-finite-sum]], with the natural exponents interpreted by [[def-integer-power]]. For the zero multi-index $0$, set $D^0f:=f$. For nonzero $\alpha$, write

$$D^\alpha f:=\partial_0^{\alpha_0}\cdots\partial_{m-1}^{\alpha_{m-1}}f$$

for this displayed, canonical order whenever it exists. Coordinate partial derivatives have the meaning fixed in [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]].

For $k\in\mathbb N$, $f$ is of class $C^k$ on $U$ when, for every word $(i_1,\ldots,i_r)$ of coordinate indices with $0\le r\le k$, the iterated derivative $\partial_{i_r}\cdots\partial_{i_1}f$ exists and is continuous on $U$; the word of length $0$ denotes $f$. Thus this definition does **not** presuppose that differently ordered derivatives are equal. Equality of their values is a later theorem under these regularity hypotheses.

before.claim: (Composition bound (a).) Fix $|\alpha|\le r\le s$ and expand $D^\alpha(F(t,\cdot,u))$ by [L3]. In each term of the expansion, by [L4] at most one factor has order $\ge r-1$; every factor of order $\le s-2$ has $L^\infty$ norm at most $C_sR$ by [L1] and the exceptional factor, of order at most $r\le s$, has $L^2$ norm at most $\|u\|_{H^s}$ by [L1]; coefficients are bounded by $M$. Hence each term has $L^2$ norm at most $M C_s^{r}(1+R)^{r}\|u\|_{H^s}^{\varepsilon}$ with $\varepsilon\in\{0,1\}$, which is at most $C_{s,R}(1+\|u\|_{H^s})$; the finitely many terms of the expansion for all $|\alpha|\le r$ give (a) after enlarging the constant.

(Difference bound (b).) For $u(t),v(t)$ with values in the convex compact $C_1$ put $u_\vartheta:=v(t)+\vartheta(u(t)-v(t))$ for $\vartheta\in[0,1]$; its values lie in $C_1\subseteq O$ and $\|u_\vartheta\|_{H^s}\le(1-\vartheta)\|v(t)\|_{H^s}+\vartheta\|u(t)\|_{H^s}\le R$. The mean-value formula $F(u)-F(v)=\int_0^1DF(t,\cdot,u_\vartheta)(u-v)\,d\vartheta$ holds pointwise and hence in $L^2$; by step 1.1 applied to the smooth coefficient $DF$, $\|DF(t,\cdot,u_\vartheta)\|_{H^{k}}\le C_R$, and by [L2] applied with the finite-measure $L^2$ bound, $\|DF(u_\vartheta)(u-v)\|_{H^{k}}\le C_R\|u-v\|_{H^{k}}$; integrating in $\vartheta$ gives (b).

(Commutator bound (c).) By the Leibniz-rule part of [L3], $[D^\alpha,A(u)]w=\sum_{0<\gamma\le\alpha}c_\gamma\,D^\gamma(A(t,\cdot,u))\,D^{\alpha-\gamma}w$. For each $\gamma\ne0$: the expansion of $D^\gamma(A(u))$ has terms with total order $|\gamma|\le k\le s$, so by [L4] each term has at most one factor of order $\ge s-1$ and the remaining factors have $L^\infty$ bounds $C_sR$; hence $\|D^\gamma(A(u))\|_2\le C_R$. Two cases exhaust the possibilities: if $|\gamma|\le s-2$, then $\sup|D^\gamma(A(t,\cdot,u))|\le C_R$ by [L1] (applied to the composition, whose $H^s$ norm is bounded by step 1.1 with $r=s$), while $\|D^{\alpha-\gamma}w\|_2\le\|w\|_{H^{|\alpha|-1}}$ because $|\alpha-\gamma|\le|\alpha|-1$; if $|\gamma|\ge s-1$, then $|\gamma|\le k=s-1$ forces $|\gamma|=s-1$ and $|\alpha-\gamma|\le k-(s-1)=0$, so $\|D^\gamma(A(u))\|_2\le C_R$ as just computed and $\|w\|_\infty\le C\|w\|_{H^{k}}$ with $k=s-1=j$ in the notation of the previous paragraph, hence at most $C\|w\|_{H^{|\alpha|-1}}$ because $|\alpha|=s-1$ in this case. Summing the finitely many terms gives (c).

(Coefficient product (d).) Fix $|\gamma|\le j\le k$ and expand $D^\gamma(A(u)w)=\sum_{\delta\le\gamma}\binom{\gamma}{\delta}D^\delta(A(u))\,D^{\gamma-\delta}w$ by [L3]. If $|\delta|\ge s-1$, then $|\delta|=s-1=k=j$ and $\delta=\gamma$, $|\gamma-\delta|=0$, so $\|D^\delta(A(u))\|_2\le C_R$ by step 1.1 with $r=k$ and $\|w\|_\infty\le\|w\|_{H^{j}}$ by [L1] with $(s,m)=(j,0)$; if $|\delta|\le s-2$ then $\sup|D^\delta(A(u))|\le C_R$ by [L1] applied to the $H^s$ class $A(u)$ (whose $H^s$ norm is bounded by step 1.1 with $r=s$) and $\|D^{\gamma-\delta}w\|_2\le\|w\|_{H^j}$. Summing the finitely many terms gives (d).

after.claim: (Localize coefficients without convexity.) Cover $K$ by finitely many balls whose doubled closed balls lie in $O$. In each doubled ball choose a smooth bump equal to $1$ on the inner ball and zero outside the doubled ball; such a radial bump is constructed from $\eta(r)=e^{-1/r}$ for $r>0$ and $0$ otherwise, whose derivatives at zero vanish since exponential decay dominates every polynomial. If these bumps are $\phi_l$, put $\chi=1-\prod_l(1-\phi_l)$. Then $\chi=1$ on a neighborhood of $K$ and has compact support in $O$. Extend $\chi F$ and $\chi A$ by zero in the value variable outside $O$. They are smooth and equal to the original coefficients near $K$. On $I_0$ times the torus times the compact convex hull of any fixed compact neighborhood of $K$, all their required derivatives are bounded. This permits line-segment arguments even when $O$ is nonconvex.

(Composition (a).) For a smooth $u$, the order-$j$ chain expansion consists of bounded coefficient derivatives times products $\prod_l D^{\beta_l}u$ with total order at most $j\le s$. At most one factor has order at least $s-1$, since $2(s-1)>s$; all others have order at most $s-2$ and are bounded in $L^\infty$ by [L1]. The possible exceptional factor has $L^2$ norm bounded by $\|u\|_{H^s}$; if there is no exceptional factor, use finite volume. Thus each term is at most $C_R(1+\|u\|_{H^s})$, proving the asserted bound. For a general Sobolev field, Fourier truncations have bounded $H^s$ norms and converge uniformly to $u$, with values eventually in a fixed compact neighborhood of $K$. Apply the smooth bound to the extension of step 1.1. Fourier coefficients of the compositions converge by uniform convergence; finite weighted Fourier sums give the same $H^s$ bound for the limit. This also identifies the weak derivative expansion by testing the smooth approximations.

(Differences (b).) With the extended coefficient and $u_\theta=v+\theta(u-v)$, the pointwise identity $F(u)-F(v)=\int_0^1 F_u(u_\theta)(u-v)\,d\theta$ holds. The maps $u_\theta$ have $H^s$ norm at most $R$ and take values in the compact convex hull of $K$. Step 2.1 applied to the extended derivative bounds $F_u(u_\theta)$ in $H^{s-1}$ uniformly. The algebra estimate [L2] gives the $H^{s-1}$ difference bound after integration. At order zero bounded $F_u$ gives the pointwise Lipschitz estimate and hence its $L^2$ version.

(Homogeneous commutators (c).) Expand $[D^\alpha,A(u)]w=\sum_{0<\gamma\le\alpha}\binom\alpha\gamma D^\gamma(A(u))D^{\alpha-\gamma}w$. For $|\gamma|\le s-2$, step 2.1 and [L1] bound the first factor in $L^\infty$; the second has at most $j-1$ derivatives. For $j\le s-1$ the only remaining case is $j=|\gamma|=s-1$, where the first factor is $L^2$ bounded and $w$ is $L^\infty$ bounded by its $H^{s-2}$ norm. For $j=s$ and $|\gamma|\ge s-1$, at most one derivative falls on $w$, which is $L^\infty$ bounded by its $H^{s-1}$ norm. These cases give precisely (c), without an additive constant. Density gives the distributional identity and bounds for general $w$.

(Multipliers (d).) In the Leibniz expansion at order $j\le s-1$, coefficient derivatives at most $s-2$ are $L^\infty$ bounded. The only remaining case is a coefficient derivative of order $s-1$, with no derivative on $w$ and $j=s-1$; its $L^2$ norm is bounded and $w$ has the required $L^\infty$ bound. Summation gives (d). Smooth approximation proves the claimed product membership for general Sobolev $w$.

(Lower-norm-controlled high estimates (e).) With $\|z\|_{H^{n-1}}\le\rho$, derivatives of $z$ of order at most $n-3$ are $L^\infty$ bounded. In the order-$n$ chain expansion at most one factor has order at least $n-2$, since $2(n-2)>n$. Its $L^2$ norm is bounded by $\rho$ unless its order is $n$, in which case it is bounded by $\|z\|_{H^n}$. This proves the high composition bound. In a commutator with $|\alpha|\le n$, a coefficient derivative of order at most $n-3$ is bounded in $L^\infty$, and the remaining derivative of $w$ has order at most $n-1$. A coefficient derivative of order at least $n-2$ has $L^2$ bound $C_\rho(1+\|z\|_{H^n})$, and at most two derivatives land on $w$; their $L^\infty$ bound follows from $w\in H^{n-2}$, since $n-4\ge2$. Sum the finite expansion. Density extends the bound as in step 2.1. All smooth derived coefficients are covered by the same argument. This proves (e).
